sections.content: How many people stayed in Skipton after gaining qualifications?

Skipton is a small town in Yorkshire and The Humber. Skipton does not have its own university.

Skipton has medium levels of deprivation.

Overall, Skipton ended up with:

  • fewer graduates than it produced
  • a similar number of non-graduates with advanced qualifications as it produced
Note: all towns and cities in this analysis are defined based on population size only. This means that some cities are classed as towns because of their population.

Let's explore this further

There were 725 state-school pupils from Skipton who sat their GCSEs between the 2007 to 2008 and the 2010 to 2011 school years.

Of these, 260 (36%) went on to gain degree-level qualifications (level 6+ as defined by The Office of Qualifications and Examinations Regulation, or Ofqual ). We will call these people graduates.

Another 245 (34%) went on to gain other advanced post-16 qualifications, such as A-Levels, a foundation degree or higher apprenticeship (levels 3-5 as defined by Ofqual). In this tool, we will refer to these non-graduates with advanced qualifications as “qualified non-graduates", for brevity.

The charts below compare Skipton to other English towns and cities using three measures:

  • what proportion of Skipton's pupils became graduates or qualified non-graduates by the 2017 to 2018 academic year
  • of those graduates and qualified non-graduates, the percentages that lived in Skipton in the 2018 to 2019 academic year
  • how many graduates and qualified non-graduates from elsewhere came to live there by 2018 to 2019, relative to the number who sat their GCSEs there

In some towns, some of this information may not be available because of small sample sizes.
The size and deprivation level of a town, as well as the qualification levels of older residents, were all related to students' educational attainment. Read our previous analysis.

Where did those who left Skipton move to?

Of Skipton's graduates, 105 were living elsewhere in 2018/19.

Of Skipton's qualified (level 3+) non-graduates, 75 were living elsewhere in 2018/19.

However, 25 of those qualified non-graduates (33%) were living fairly locally, in the Skipton travel to work area (TTWA).

Of those in Skipton's GCSE cohort:

  • 70 graduates left Yorkshire and The Humber
  • 30 qualified (level 3+) non-graduates left Yorkshire and The Humber

In 2018 to 2019, 37% of graduates and 35% of qualified non-graduates living in Skipton had moved there from elsewhere

In the 2018 to 2019 academic year, there were 230 graduates and 245 qualified (level 3+) non-graduates from our cohort living in Skipton. This is compared with the 260 graduates and 245 qualified non-graduates who had lived there when they sat their GCSEs.

In 2018 to 2019, 63% of the graduates had also lived in Skipton as GCSE pupils, while 37% had moved there from elsewhere.

Of the qualified non-graduates who lived in Skipton in 2018 to 2019, 67% had lived there as GCSE pupils, while 35% had moved to the area from elsewhere.
